## What is WENDy?

WENDy (**W**eak-form **E**stimation of **N**onlinear **Dy**namics) estimates the
parameters of an ODE system $\dot u = f(u, p, t)$ directly from noisy data —
without ever running a forward solver. The trick is the *weak form*: multiply
the ODE by smooth, compactly supported test functions $\varphi_k$ and integrate
by parts,

$$
\int \varphi_k \, \dot u \, dt \;=\; -\int \dot\varphi_k \, u \, dt,
$$

so the derivative lands on the analytic test function instead of the noisy
data. Discretizing these integrals over the data grid produces a residual
system in $p$ alone — no numerical differentiation of the data, no ODE
integration, and no initial condition needed for the parameter estimate.
`method = "MLE"` minimizes a weak-form negative log-likelihood whose
covariance accounts for how the measurement noise propagates through the
test-function quadrature.

Because integration by parts eliminates $u_0$ from the fit, the initial
condition has to be recovered *after* $\hat p$ is found. Two controls do that:

- `estimate_IC = TRUE` — estimates $\hat u_0$ (BLDC: boundary-layer data
  correction) using test functions clustered at $t = 0$ with Euler–Maclaurin
  boundary corrections, holding $\hat p$ fixed.
- `estimate_trajectory = TRUE` — runs an extended Rauch–Tung–Striebel smoother
  (ERTS) with the fitted dynamics, returning a smoothed trajectory
  $U^\star$ and a posterior covariance that folds parameter uncertainty into
  the state uncertainty (law of total variance).

## 1. Simulate the logistic model

Logistic growth, $\dot u = p_1 u - p_2 u^2$, with true parameters
$p^\star = (1, 1/10)$ — i.e. growth rate $r = 1$ and carrying capacity
$K = p_1/p_2 = 10$ — starting from $u_0 = 0.1$. webR has no `deSolve`, but
none is needed: the logistic equation has the closed-form solution

$$
u(t) = \frac{K}{1 + \left(K/u_0 - 1\right) e^{-r t}},
$$

which is exact (no integrator tolerance to worry about).

```{webr}
# RHS in the f(u, p, t) form that solveWendy() expects
f <- function(u, p, t) {
  c(p[1] * u[1] - p[2] * u[1]^2)
}

p_star  <- c(1, 1/10)   # true parameters: r = 1, K = p1/p2 = 10
u0      <- 0.1          # true initial condition
npoints <- 64
t_span  <- c(0, 10)
t_eval  <- seq(t_span[1], t_span[2], length.out = npoints)

# Closed-form logistic solution (replaces a deSolve forward solve)
logistic_sol <- function(t, p, u0) {
  r <- p[1]; K <- p[1] / p[2]
  K / (1 + (K / u0 - 1) * exp(-r * t))
}

u_true <- logistic_sol(t_eval, p_star, u0)
```

## 2. Corrupt the data with noise

We add i.i.d. Gaussian noise at a 25% *noise ratio*: the noise standard
deviation is `nr` times the RMS level of the clean signal, so the corruption
scales with the trajectory rather than being an arbitrary absolute value.
This is substantial noise — note in particular how unreliable the first
observation becomes as an estimate of $u_0$.

```{webr}
set.seed(8675309 + 8)

nr <- 0.25  # noise ratio: sd as a fraction of the RMS signal level

# Additive Gaussian noise
noise_sd <- nr * sqrt(mean(u_true^2))
U  <- matrix(u_true + rnorm(npoints, mean = 0, sd = noise_sd), ncol = 1)
tt <- matrix(t_eval, ncol = 1)

# Multiplicative log-normal noise (alternative; then pass
# noise_dist = "lognormal" to solveWendy):
# U <- matrix(u_true * exp(rnorm(npoints, mean = 0, sd = nr)), ncol = 1)

cat(sprintf("σ = %.2f", noise_sd))
```

## 3. Fit with WENDy

One call does all three jobs: estimate $\hat p$ by weak-form MLE, recover
$\hat u_0$ from the boundary layer, and smooth the full state with the ERTS
filter.

```{webr}
time <- system.time({
  res <- solveWendy(f, U, tt, method = "MLE",
    control = list(
      estimate_IC         = TRUE,
      estimate_trajectory = TRUE
    )
  )
})

cat(sprintf("p̂  = [%s]   rel_err = %.4f\n",
            paste(sprintf("%.4f", res$phat), collapse = ", "),
            rel_err(res$phat, p_star)))
cat(sprintf("û₀ = %.4f   (true u₀ = %.1f, noisy observation = %.4f)\n",
            res$u0hat, u0, U[1, 1]))
print(time)
```

## 4. Smoothed state and the initial condition

The plot compares three candidates for $u_0$ against the truth: the raw noisy
observation $U_1$ (green), the BLDC estimate $\hat u_0$ (blue), and the first
point of the ERTS-smoothed trajectory (orange). The shaded band is the
$\pm 2$ SE ERTS posterior — total uncertainty, i.e. the conditional-on-$\hat p$
posterior plus the parameter uncertainty propagated through the trajectory
sensitivities.

```{webr}
# Dense true trajectory for reference (closed form again — no solver needed)
t_dense  <- seq(t_span[1], t_span[2], length.out = 400)
sol_true <- logistic_sol(t_dense, p_star, u0)

U_star    <- res$state$U_star
u0hat     <- res$u0hat
u0_smooth <- U_star[1, 1]
tt_vec    <- as.vector(tt)

# Total posterior SE from ERTS: conditional-on-p̂ posterior + parameter
# uncertainty folded in via the trajectory sensitivity (law of total variance).
se_post <- sqrt(res$state$P_smooth[, 1, 1])

band_post_lo <- U_star[, 1] - 2 * se_post
band_post_hi <- U_star[, 1] + 2 * se_post

ylim <- range(c(U, band_post_lo, band_post_hi), finite = TRUE)
plot(t_dense, sol_true, col = "red", type = "l",
     xlab = "Time", ylab = "u₁", ylim = ylim)
polygon(c(tt_vec, rev(tt_vec)), c(band_post_lo, rev(band_post_hi)),
        col = adjustcolor("#1f77b4", alpha.f = 0.25), border = NA)
lines(tt_vec, U_star[, 1], col = "#1f77b4", lwd = 2)
points(tt, U, col = "black", cex = 0.5)
points(tt[1], u0hat,     pch = 17, col = "#1f77b4", cex = 1)
points(tt[1], u0_smooth, pch = 17, col = "#ff7f0e", cex = 1)
points(tt[1], U[1, 1],   pch = 17, col = "green",   cex = 1)

title(paste0("nr: ", nr, "   n: ", npoints,
             "   p̂: ", round(res$phat[1], 3), " ", round(res$phat[2], 3)))

legend(
  "bottomright",
  legend = c("true trajectory", "smoothed state (ERTS)",
             "±2 SE (ERTS posterior)",
             "û₀ BLDC", "û₀ ERTS",
             "u₀ noisy"),
  col    = c("red", "#1f77b4",
             adjustcolor("#1f77b4", alpha.f = 0.6),
             "#1f77b4", "#ff7f0e", "green"),
  pch    = c(NA, NA, 15, 17, 17, 17),
  lty    = c(1, 1, NA, NA, NA, NA),
  xpd    = TRUE,
  bty    = "n",
  cex    = 0.7
)
```
